decisions.executionNote: Begin a gradual elbow-up approach toward the left standing white bottle; keep right arm parked and both grippers open.

Continue pitching down above the lying white bottle while advancing the wrist, preserving elbow-up continuity.

Close around the lying white bottle and lift slightly to test whether the body is retained.

Ease the wrist pitch to avoid the rejected configuration while shifting the open grasp leftward onto the bottle.
Align the finger midpoint with the visible bottle body and descend carefully before closing.
Advance the open grasp toward the bottle instead of closing behind it; ease pitch to preserve joint continuity.
Adjust the oblique approach forward while easing wrist pitch, aiming to surround the white bottle rather than push its near edge.
Lift clear and change jaw direction to grip across the bottle's width rather than along its length.
Reorient toward a transverse top grasp and move over the white bottle while keeping clearance.

Translate the oblique open grasp left, forward, and down onto the visible white bottle body; hold orientation fixed.
Advance the open fingers forward and right to the bottle's current position, avoiding further downward contact.
Relax the downward wrist angle while lowering the wrist, keeping the open fingertips near the bottle and away from the rejected joint configuration.
Bring the open fingers forward to the white bottle's body at its new position, holding grasp height and orientation.
Ease the wrist angle instead of advancing into the rejected configuration, shifting left to keep the finger midpoint aligned with the bottle.
Use the wrist view to center the white bottle between the jaws, moving diagonally left and forward with a shallower approach.
Back away from the reach boundary and correct the fingertip midpoint rightward using the head view; keep fingers open.
Close at the bottle's current position and make a short upward/backward retention test, judging the result visually.
The grasp is empty. Reopen and shift the jaws forward toward the bottle, with a small left and downward correction.
Retract from the continuity boundary while turning the open gripper toward the bottle on the left of the wrist view.
Center the bottle in the wrist view by continuing a gentle yaw adjustment and lowering the open grasp.
The body is now between the visible jaws. Close without translation, then test retention with a small lift and retreat.
The fingers closed above the bottle. Reopen, move right to its body center, and lower the grasp plane before retrying.
Seat the open jaws slightly farther around the bottle, close in place, and test with a small lift.
Keep the jaws closed and lift back from the table to check retention before transporting toward the bin.
The bottle remains on the table. Lower the reopened grasp substantially and shift toward the narrower neck for another secure grasp attempt.
Turn the jaws obliquely across the bottle rather than along its length, keeping the grasp near the body and lowering to its sides.
Withdraw the left arm from the difficult far bottle and begin a gradual right-arm approach to the nearer upright thermos.
Continue withdrawing the left arm; turn the right open gripper inward and approach the thermos from its right-front side.
Bring the open right fingers around the thermos body with a modest inward turn; park the left arm farther back.
Thermos has toppled. Lift the right wrist clear while gradually pitching down for a grasp across its lying body.
Retry from the unchanged pose with half-sized pitch and translation increments to preserve joint continuity.
Thermos rolled into the left workspace. Clear the right arm and bring the left hand around to approach its exposed end without crossing arms.
Align the left gripper along the lying thermos, approaching its cap end with jaws open and gradually lowering to bottle height.
Use smaller increments after the guard: lower and shift the left open fingers toward the thermos while completing a level end-on alignment.

Lift the thermos with the left gripper closed and move slightly toward the bin; check that it follows before release.

Lower the fingers to the thermos midline and deepen the insertion a little, then close and pause before a small retention lift.
Lift and draw the closed left grasp toward the bin, checking for bottle motion with the gripper.

The wrist met the table. Raise slightly, shift the jaw midpoint toward the near side of the thermos, and close at this lower height.
Keep the thermos grasp closed and lift slowly while drawing left; move the right hand clear and verify bottle retention visually.

Reduce pitch and lift increments after the zero-step rejection, preserving the current elbow-up configuration.
Continue the overhead approach in small increments, leaving the right hand clear.
Pitch the open left fingers down over the thermos while keeping the wrist elevated and shifting the grasp toward its center.
Lower the top grasp onto the thermos body, close across its width, and test retention with a small lift.

Retry a centered top pinch with a slightly higher contact plane and gradual closure, avoiding the previous abrupt squeeze.
Allow the closed grasp to settle without sliding, then make a slow vertical retention test.

Close from the lower grasp plane with fingers beside the thermos, settle, then lift straight up to verify retention.
The closed fingertips still pass above the bottle. Reopen and descend farther with fixed alignment to reach its sides.
Close with the jaws now visibly down beside the thermos, settle, and lift vertically to check retention.

Carry the visibly retained thermos toward the left bin, gently turning the wrist while keeping the gripper closed.
Continue leftward over the dustbin, rotating the retained thermos to keep its full length clear of the table edge.
Release the thermos over the bin and withdraw. Begin a slow right-arm reorientation for the lying yellow bottle.

Continue the right overhead approach and downward pitch; park the left hand clear of the handover area.
Refine the right top grasp with smaller increments and descend beside the yellow bottle, keeping the left hand stationary.

Recenter the right jaws slightly right around the yellow bottle, close at its sides, and make a small vertical retention test.
Lift the yellow bottle with the right grip held closed and retreat slightly; verify that it follows before arranging a handover.
